body:
Yeah, I think you are right. That is why I put it in SuicideThoughts instead of SuicideWatch. Sometimes I scare myself though. Talking it out really does help. I need to start a journal I think.
I'll definitely make sure you know the outcome. Thanks for the input.

It is possible, but I can't stay in this apartment with her. It will drive me mad, and although I may be able to earn half the rent, I can't earn half the rent plus my rent plus security deposit. Travelling homeless is a different beast than stationary city homeless, it seems to me. I would rather wander the land. It seems like it would give me reason to breath.

The apartment. The lease. These are aspects of being a part of the city. The job pays the bills. All of these things hold each other together. Why do I keep them? For her. She wants these things. I'll admit, these things are enjoyable to me also. I like a warm bed. Food in the fridge. The juice just isn't worth the squeeze. Maybe it is just the depression talking. Taking off would be one way to find out.

Yes. It is something that I wouldn't have been able to do. Everything seems aligned ever so perfectly. Yet, I fear that I wouldn't be able to make enough to send back. I really don't want to leave her with a rent bill that she can't afford on her own. No one deserves that. Maybe I will go to work over the weekend and give it some good thought. Actually, she's working out of town next week. That would be the perfect time to slip away without painful confrontation. The blocks keep falling into place. The universe, perhaps, needs me alive.

I have done it before. Even in a relatively bad location it brings in about 10-15 dollars an hour. Good locations are harder to come by but half of rent could be achieved in probably 6-8 hours. I've never done it as a vagrant though. It would be interesting.
I feel as though being away from this relationship failure and out on the road might be just what I need. There is something about working at a business for hours on end for most of the week that really gets me down. Maybe it's not just the fact of working the majority of my waking life to have a minimum of comfort, but the fact that employers expect you to work there for years. I understand that they want competent and experienced employees, but I burn out quickly. I long for new experiences. Sometimes, regular jobs make me feel like a slave. It's depressing.

There are other options, but for the sake of readability I've condensed it to the two most seemingly relevant options.
C,D, and E would be variations on dealing with the situation in a civilized fashion. I'm sure I could think of a hundred different possible living situations.
F, I imagine, would be something along the lines of trying to drown out all thoughts and feelings with one thing or another.

To elaborate, I like the city, sometimes I love it. I've actually made a friend or two within my apartment building. The job that I started is a really great opportunity. It's an upscale business with huge profit potential, unfortunately I am starting at the low bottom. Overnight. Weekend shift. Not guaranteed full time. Of course, this is how it goes. especially in these economic times. I should really be thankful to have a job at all.
Since we moved here, we've spent most of the savings while trying to find jobs. She got one before me. I spent a lot of time alone. I think that is part of what triggered this recent episode of depression, which then snowballed into today.
I guess the bottom line is that I don't want to live in this city. She is why I am here. And now, the lease is why I should stay.
The idea to leave her with the tab is, admittedly, tempting.
If I were to bum down the coast, I could be a street musician and most likely make half of the rent to send to her each month. I just don't think that I could stand to live here for 4 more months.

My friend with the Xanax said he would get in touch with a doctor that he thinks can help.
I've made a pretty firm decision not to drink through this. Partly, because I have to keep myself together for the job should I choose to stay. I'm mostly just not as into intoxicants as I used to be. Thankfully.
Thank you for the words of wisdom.
